result_text:
Template literals are now emptied before units are compared for duplication, so two JavaScript functions that differ only inside a `` `...` `` literal are reported as one duplicated unit. The JavaScript and C-style extractor tests pass, including a new one. I did not run the other modules' tests or an end-to-end duplication report.

- **Change:** I overrode `extraCleanContent` in `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java` (`codeanalyzer/.../lang/js/`). It turns each `` `…` `` literal, including `${...}` parts and multi-line literals, into ` `` `. It keeps the original line breaks so line numbers stay correct, then calls the existing cleaning.
- **Scope:** I kept the change to the JavaScript extractor on purpose. Backticks mean something else in Kotlin, Scala and Go (identifiers and raw strings), so changing the shared C-style code could have altered those. If TypeScript uses a different extractor, it isn't covered. I didn't check which one it uses.
- **Test:** `templateLiteralsAreEmptiedInCleanedBody` in `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest` checks two things. Functions that differ only in the literal text get the same cleaned body. A difference outside the literal (`` + 1 ``) keeps them different.

I haven't committed anything.
